newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Clarke says UK government won't change EMU policy.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says UK government won't change EMU policy.

text.p: There is no chance of the British government changing its mind on its policy on whether to join the European monetary union (EMU), with a decision to be made only if it is clear the country will benefit, UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday.

"There is not the slightest prospect of the government changing its mind...it's been our policy for a very long time," he told reporters in Bermuda where he is attending a Commonwealth finance ministers conference.

Clarke repeated charges that comments he made at the weekend had been misinterpreted to suggest that he was at odds over cabinet policy on EMU, which is not to make a decision until the single currency is launched.

"It not only is it our policy, it is the only sensible policy. We will have to make our minds up when the time comes, in the light of what matters to British jobs, and British industry and our future prosperity," Clarke said.
He denied he had called Britian's policy pathetic, reports of which earlier this week sparked fury among right-wingers in the ruling party, some suggesting he should resign.
